method.method_draft: From the text, take the DC part of the base current as I_BQ = 1 mA and ignore the sinusoidal small-signal component for bias calculation. Write r_pi = beta/g_m. Substitute g_m = I_CQ/V_T and I_CQ = beta I_BQ, giving r_pi = beta /(beta I_BQ/V_T) = V_T/I_BQ. With V_T = 25 mV at 300 K, r_pi = 25 mV / 1 mA = 25 ohms.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The attached circuit diagram shows the small-signal hybrid-pi model of an NPN transistor. The base terminal B has the input current i_b entering it, r_pi is connected between base B and emitter E, and the emitter is grounded. On the collector side, a dependent current source and r_o are connected between collector C and emitter E.

Reasoning: The given base current is i_b = 1 + 0.1 cos(10000 pi t) mA. For the bias calculation, take only the DC component, so I_BQ = 1 mA. In the small-signal model, r_pi = beta / g_m. Since g_m = I_CQ / V_T and I_CQ = beta I_BQ, we get r_pi = beta / (beta I_BQ / V_T) = V_T / I_BQ. At 300 K for silicon, V_T is approximately 25 mV. Therefore r_pi = 25 mV / 1 mA = 25 ohms.
